candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity: assess changes in psychosocial functioning, use therapeutic communication, support coping, and address stressors associated with illness and hospitalization.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — psychological effects of isolation precautions
candidate.educational_objective: While maintaining indicated transmission-based precautions, assess for isolation-related psychosocial distress and reduce it through clear education, therapeutic communication, regular human contact, dignity, and referral/support when needed.

options.A: Acknowledge the distress, explain the reason for precautions, maintain regular therapeutic contact and communication, and assess whether additional psychosocial support is needed.
options.B: Tell the client that isolation has no recognized psychological effects and that discussing anxiety may make adjustment more difficult.
options.C: Minimize staff contact beyond essential procedures because reducing interaction is part of the purpose of transmission-based precautions.
options.D: Discontinue the required isolation precautions solely because the client reports loneliness and anxiety.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Nursing infection-control guidance recognizes that isolation precautions can be associated with anxiety, depression, anger, loneliness, and stigma in some hospitalized clients. Education about the reason for precautions, emotional preparation, communication, and psychological support can reduce distress while infection-prevention measures remain in place. B dismisses a recognized potential effect. C unnecessarily compounds social isolation; precautions limit infection transmission, not therapeutic communication. D is unsafe because psychosocial distress should be addressed without independently discontinuing clinically indicated precautions.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Isolation precautions may contribute to psychological distress in some clients; nurses should preserve indicated infection-control measures while providing education, communication, dignity and psychosocial support.
candidate.source_locator: Chapter 9 Infection — 'Psychological Effects of Isolation': transmission-based precautions can negatively affect mental well-being and behavior, including depression, anxiety, anger and stigma; client/family education when precautions begin is critical to reduce anxiety/distress, and preparing clients emotionally helps coping. WHO/NCBI infection-prevention guidance also notes possible social isolation, depression or anxiety during prolonged single-room isolation and recommends communication, dignity, respect and psychological support.
candidate.source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
candidate.stem: A client has been on transmission-based isolation precautions for several days and says, 'I feel cut off from everyone and more anxious each day.' Which nursing response is most appropriate?
